title: DBSCAN
description: Density-based spatial clustering algorithm for grouping close points and identifying noise.
name: DBSCAN
summary: DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) groups points that are close to each other based on distance and minimum neighbor counts, marking low-density outlier points as noise.
use_when: Clustering data with arbitrary/irregular shapes and identifying anomalies/noise points without setting K.
avoid_when: Working with clusters of highly varying densities or in very high-dimensional feature spaces.
pros: Does not require pre-specifying the number of clusters.
Can discover clusters of arbitrary shapes (e.g. nested rings).
Natively isolates noise and outlier points from valid clusters.
cons: Cannot cluster datasets with large variations in density effectively.
Highly sensitive to the distance threshold parameter eps.
Performs poorly in high-dimensional spaces due to distance metrics collapsing.

key_hyperparams.name: eps
key_hyperparams.note: The maximum distance between two samples for one to be considered as in the neighborhood of the other.

quick_start:
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1, 2], [2, 2], [2, 3], [8, 7], [8, 8], [25, 80]])
clustering = DBSCAN(eps=3, min_samples=2).fit(X)
labels = clustering.labels_
